item.title: CBS News Radio to end in May, 700 affiliates scrambling for new national programming
item.description: The move reflects broader challenges facing radio amid competition from streaming audio and digital platforms.

item.title: Bars, restaurants may lose access to NFL Sunday Ticket
item.description: The change follows the end of a temporary deal allowing DIRECTV to offer the package to business customers.

item.title: States ask federal court to issue restraining order blocking Nexstar-TEGNA deal
item.description: Officials argue the merger violates antitrust laws and prioritizes corporate interests over consumers.

item.title: Scripps to launch free streaming network for Scripps Sports
item.description: March 23, 2026 - The E. W. Scripps Company is readying the launch of a new free, ad-supported streaming television (FAST) channel focused on its Scripps Sports programming.

item.title: Roku partners with Google on identity, measurement capabilities for advertisers
item.description: Roku is partnering with Google as a launch partner for its Confidential Publisher Match identity solution in Display & Video 360.

item.title: Hearst promotes Christopher Martinez to VP, Advanced Advertising
item.description: Hearst Television has promoted Christopher Martinez to the newly created role of Vice President, Advanced Advertising.

item.title: Charter names John Lee as Head of Intelligence Ventures
item.description: Charter Communications has named John Lee as Head of Intelligence Ventures, establishing a new leadership role focused on developing data- and AI-driven products and partnerships.

item.title: What makes a streaming service unique? Viewers don't know, Hub survey reveals
item.description: A new consumer survey from Hub Entertainment Research finds that most streamers are unable to explain clearly to others what separates one service from another.

item.title: Nexstar to operate TEGNA as subsidiary business while lawsuits proceed
item.description: The move will allow Nexstar to spin-out TEGNA if lawsuits are successful; on Monday, Newsmax and several broadband groups filed a request for a preliminary injunction.

item.title: Gray Media gets FCC approval to acquire Allen Media TV stations
item.description: The FCC has approved the transfer of 10 local television broadcast licenses from Allen Media Group to peer broadcaster Gray Media.
